turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I just can't seem to stop launching projects lately. It's like my brain is just churning out work plans, new certification schedules for my team, completely overhauling my home network... which, by the way, if you ever use the default router your ISP gives you, you're practically begging for a security breach. I was actually explaining this to my neighbor, Dave, just the other night because his Wi-Fi channel was interfering with my new mesh setup. Dave's a good guy, he really is, but he still uses a password he made in 1999 for his dog that died ten years ago. It's wild how little people care about data privacy. 

But anyway, yeah, I've just been doing all that, plus messaging all these old contacts on LinkedIn, trying to get these massive ideas off the ground. And it just gets so intense. I just blow past all the normal limits, you know? I don't even realize I'm doing it until my wife or my director at work has to actually step in and tell me to hit the brakes. Which is why my wife made me come talk to you, honestly.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a significant increase in goal-directed activities, such as launching numerous work projects, overhauling a home network, and messaging old contacts, to the point where others have to intervene.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any unusual thoughts, hearing voices, or feeling like people are trying to communicate special messages to you that others might not understand?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no voices. But special messages... yeah, actually. I mean, I pick up on things that other people just completely miss. 

Like at work, even when I’m not in one of those big mood swings where I'm launching a million projects, I still notice these... signs. I'll get completely convinced that certain calendar invites that don't have an agenda attached, or the way someone's Microsoft Teams status suddenly changes to "Do Not Disturb" the second I log on, or just weird passing comments in the hallway... I get convinced they're these coded warnings. Like they are all secretly coordinating and building a case to push me out of the company. 

Which makes zero sense because I literally designed our entire cloud migration strategy. Do you know how hard it is to migrate a legacy on-prem server to AWS without any downtime? It’s a nightmare. My lead engineer, Greg, he wanted to do it over a holiday weekend, which sounds smart until you realize AWS support is on a skeleton crew then. Greg means well, he really does, but he still uses a trackball mouse. I don't know how anyone gets any real work done with a trackball, it just seems so incredibly inefficient. I tried one back in college and my wrist hurt for a week. I actually had to wear a brace during my database management finals... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the messages. But yeah, I just... I get this intense feeling that they're using the very communication systems I set up to secretly plot against me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes fixed, paranoid beliefs that coworkers are using calendar invites and Teams statuses as coded warnings to secretly plot against them.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from workplace paranoia to cloud migration, a coworker's trackball mouse, and college finals before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient mentions experiencing 'big mood swings.'
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient references past periods of 'launching a million projects,' indicating episodes of increased goal-directed activity.

turns.doctor_question: Are you still feeling convinced that your coworkers are plotting against you even when you are not in one of those high-energy, project-launching moods?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, definitely. There have been several stretches, sometimes lasting a few weeks at a time, where I'm just... flat. Not hyped up on projects, not depressed, just totally calm. But even then, I still absolutely believe the Teams statuses are coded warnings. 

Which, speaking of Teams, Microsoft pushed an update last Tuesday that completely messed up the presence indicators across our whole tenant. Half my team was showing as 'Offline' when they were actively pushing code to the repository. I had to write a custom PowerShell script just to force-sync the Azure AD tokens. PowerShell is honestly a lifesaver, though a lot of the younger devs just want to use Python for everything now. I mean, Python is great for data modeling, but for system administration? Come on, you need native OS integration. 

But anyway, yeah, even during those quiet weeks, I know they're plotting. And actually... earlier I said I didn't hear voices. I guess that's not entirely accurate now that I think about it. Because during those same calm stretches, I'll hear these brief comments, like someone saying something right behind my chair, but when I turn around, no one is there. 

I thought maybe it was the HVAC system at first. Our office building has terrible ductwork. They installed these cheap acoustic panels last year that do absolutely nothing to dampen the sound. I told the facilities manager, Linda, that she needed to look into high-density fiberglass, but she just bought whatever was on sale in bulk. Linda's nice, she always brings in donuts on Fridays, but she doesn't understand acoustics at all... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the moods. Yeah, the warnings and the comments happen even when my mood is completely level.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that coworkers are plotting against them and that Teams statuses are coded warnings.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient reports hearing brief comments from someone right behind their chair when no one is actually there.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting into unrelated topics like PowerShell, Python, HVAC systems, and a coworker's donuts before returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the times when you feel high-energy or when you are feeling 'flat' or calm, have you ever experienced periods where you felt deeply sad, hopeless, or lacked the energy to do anything at all?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. There are definitely times, like... stretches where I just wake up feeling like this completely failed version of myself. Just incredibly heavy and... I don't know, flat isn't even the right word, it's more like being drained of every single drop of motivation. Even just answering my wife's normal, everyday questions feels like it takes a monumental amount of effort. 

It's actually kind of like when a server's CPU usage is maxed out at 99% and it just stops responding to basic ping requests. You know, we had a server do exactly that last month because one of the junior devs wrote an infinite loop in a background processing job. I swear, they don't teach memory management in bootcamps anymore. They just teach them how to string together APIs and call it a day. I had to manually kill the process at 3 AM on a Tuesday. And honestly, waking up at 3 AM is the absolute worst because your circadian rhythm is right in the middle of its deep sleep phase. I read this fascinating article about sleep cycles in a neurobiology journal... they were saying that interrupting REM sleep can actually impair your cognitive function for up to 48 hours. Which explains why I was so irritable the next day when I had to explain to the dev why his code crashed our entire staging environment. 

But... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling sad. Yeah, when I get like that, when I'm just so heavy and hopeless, I can barely even look at a computer screen, let alone fix someone else's broken code.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality, drifting from discussing his mood to server CPUs, coding bootcamps, and sleep cycles before losing his train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient confirms experiencing periods of feeling 'heavy and hopeless' and 'sad'.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient describes feeling 'drained of every single drop of motivation' and states that basic tasks take a 'monumental amount of effort'.
symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient describes waking up feeling like a 'completely failed version of myself', indicating feelings of worthlessness.

turns.doctor_question: During your life, have you ever experienced these periods of feeling deeply sad and hopeless at the same time that you were also feeling that your coworkers were plotting against you?
turns.patient_response:
At the same time? I'm not really sure. I haven't really kept track of whether they overlap exactly like that. 

Time tracking is actually a huge issue for us right now at work, to be honest. We use Jira for all our sprint planning, and trying to get the developers to log their hours accurately is like pulling teeth. They'll just dump eight hours into a single ticket on Friday afternoon instead of logging it daily as they work. It completely messes up our burndown charts. And if your burndown chart is wrong, you can't accurately predict your velocity for the next sprint. 

I tried implementing this automated time-tracking plugin to make it easier for them, but it integrates directly with our IDEs, and everyone complained it felt like spyware. Which is completely ridiculous, because it's just polling active window titles, it's not keylogging. I know a thing or two about keyloggers, actually. Back when I was a teenager, I accidentally downloaded one from a sketchy gaming forum while trying to get a mod for Half-Life. It took me three days to scrub it out of the Windows registry. The registry is such a convoluted mess, honestly, Microsoft really should have rebuilt it from the ground up when they moved to the NT architecture instead of just patching over it for the last twenty years... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, the sad periods and the plotting. Yeah, I honestly couldn't tell you if they happen on the exact same days. I just haven't really noticed if they sync up.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient acknowledges experiencing feelings of coworkers plotting against them, though they are unsure if these occur concurrently with sad periods.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's response demonstrates tangentiality, drifting from the question to Jira, keyloggers, and the Windows registry before returning to the original topic.

Coffee stopped working after day two, so I switched to those energy drinks that taste like battery acid. Did you know they put taurine in those? It's an amino acid originally isolated from bull bile.
